examples.en: I doodled in my notebook during class.
I jotted down whatever came to mind on a memo pad.
I was scribbling on paper without thinking while on the phone.

examples.ko: 일기장에 하고 싶은 말을 끄적거리면 마음이 편해져요.
examples.en: Scribbling what I want to say in my diary makes me feel at ease.
What are you scribbling so much? Show me.

examples.ko: 시를 쓴다기보다 그냥 몇 줄 끄적거린 거예요.
examples.en: I didn't really write a poem. I just scribbled a few lines.

explain: 글씨나 그림을 정성 들이지 않고 아무렇게나 쓰거나 그리는 모습이에요. 그래서 스스로 쓴 글을 겸손하게 '그냥 끄적거린 거예요'라고 말할 때도 써요. '끼적거리다'와 거의 같게 쓰여요.
explain_en: It describes writing or drawing carelessly, without putting much effort in. That is why people also use it modestly about their own writing, as in '그냥 끄적거린 거예요'. It is used almost the same way as '끼적거리다'.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 공책 구석에 낙서를 끼적였어요.
examples.en: I doodled in the corner of my notebook during class.

examples.ko: 생각나는 대로 메모지에 몇 자 끼적여 봤어요.
examples.en: I scribbled a few words on a memo pad as they came to mind.

examples.ko: 그는 심심하면 영수증 뒤에 뭔가를 끼적여요.
examples.en: When he is bored, he scribbles something on the back of a receipt.

examples.ko: 기분이 안 좋을 때 일기장에 끼적이면 마음이 풀려요.
examples.en: When I feel down, scribbling in my diary makes me feel better.
The child is scribbling something on the wall.
I fell asleep with a phone number scribbled on the back of my hand.

explain: 정성껏 쓰는 '쓰다'와 달리, 글씨나 그림을 대충 가볍게 쓸 때 어울려요. '끼적거리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요. 메모, 낙서, 짧은 글을 편하게 쓰는 장면에서 잘 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike '쓰다', which can mean careful writing, this fits writing or drawing casually and roughly. '끼적거리다' is used with the same meaning. It shows up often for notes, doodles and short pieces written offhand.

examples.en: I bought a practical cookbook.

examples.ko: 이 서점에서는 실용서가 소설보다 더 잘 팔려요.
examples.en: At this bookstore, practical books sell better than novels.

examples.ko: 저는 소설보다 생활에 도움이 되는 실용서를 자주 읽어요.
examples.en: I often read practical books that help in daily life rather than novels.
Practical books about personal finance are very popular these days.

examples.ko: 실용서는 읽고 나서 바로 따라 해 볼 수 있어서 좋아요.
examples.en: I like practical books because you can try what they say right after reading.
I borrowed a practical computer book from the library.

explain: 요리, 재테크, 컴퓨터처럼 읽고 바로 따라 할 수 있는 내용을 다룬 책에 써요. '교양서'는 지식을 넓히는 책, '실용서'는 따라 해서 써먹는 책이라고 생각하면 쉬워요.
explain_en: It is used for books on cooking, personal finance or computers that you can follow and use right away. Think of a '교양서' (general-interest book) as one that broadens knowledge, and a '실용서' as one you follow and put to use.

examples.ko: 제가 악필이라서 메모를 남에게 못 보여 줘요.
examples.en: My handwriting is bad, so I can't show my notes to others.
I had a hard time reading my friend's messy handwriting.
I started practicing writing to fix my bad handwriting.

examples.ko: 악필이라서 제 글씨를 저도 못 읽어요.
examples.en: My handwriting is so bad that even I can't read it.

examples.ko: 손으로 쓸 일이 줄어서 악필이 더 심해졌어요.
examples.en: I write by hand less now, so my handwriting got even worse.
Even bad handwriting can get prettier with effort.

explain: 글씨를 알아보기 힘들게 쓰는 것을 말하고, 자기 글씨를 두고 '저 악필이에요'라고 웃으며 말하는 일이 많아요. 반대로 글씨를 잘 쓰면 '달필'이라고 하고, 아주 잘 쓰는 사람은 '명필'이라고 해요. '글씨를 못 쓰다'는 더 평범한 표현이에요.
explain_en: It means writing so messily that it is hard to read, and people often joke about their own handwriting with '저 악필이에요'. The opposite is '달필' for good handwriting, and '명필' for someone who writes exceptionally well. '글씨를 못 쓰다' is a plainer way to say it.

examples.en: I had my initials engraved on the bag.
Please write just the initials of your name first.

examples.ko: 이니셜이 같은 사람이 반에 두 명 있어요.
examples.en: There are two people in my class with the same initials.
I signed with my English initials.
I embroidered my initials on a handkerchief.
The article showed only initials instead of the name.

explain: 영어 이름의 첫 글자를 말할 때가 많아요. 한글 이름의 첫 자음은 '초성'이라고 하고, 'ㄱㄷㅈ'처럼 자음만 써요. 뉴스에서 실명을 숨길 때 'K씨'처럼 이니셜을 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It mostly means the first letters of a name written in the Roman alphabet. For Korean names, the first consonants are called '초성', written as consonants only like 'ㄱㄷㅈ'. News articles sometimes hide real names with initials, as in 'K씨'.

examples.en: I bought the magazine's first issue as a keepsake.
The first issue carried a greeting from the editor-in-chief.

examples.ko: 이 신문의 창간호는 박물관에 전시돼 있어요.
examples.en: This newspaper's first issue is on display in a museum.

examples.ko: 창간호 가격이 다른 호보다 훨씬 싸요.
examples.en: The first issue is much cheaper than the other issues.

examples.ko: 창간호부터 지금까지 모두 모은 사람이 있어요.
examples.en: There is someone who has collected every issue from the first one until now.

examples.ko: 동아리 소식지 창간호를 이번 달에 내요.
examples.en: We are putting out the first issue of the club newsletter this month.

explain: 잡지나 신문을 처음 낸 호를 말해요. 반대로 마지막 호는 '종간호'라고 해요. 그냥 '1호'라고 해도 되지만 '창간호'는 기념이나 의미가 있는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It is the very first issue of a magazine or newspaper, and the last issue is called '종간호'. You could just say '1호' (issue no. 1), but '창간호' carries a feeling of commemoration and significance.

examples.en: Please tell me the spelling of this word.
English spelling is difficult.
I got the spelling wrong and lost points.
Dictation is good for practicing spelling.
Please check if the spelling of the name is correct.
I found the typos with the spell check function.

explain: '철자'는 글자를 어떻게 쓰는지를 말해요. 한국어에서는 '맞춤법'을 더 자주 쓰는데, 맞춤법은 쓰는 규칙 전체이고 철자는 한 단어를 어떻게 쓰는지에 가까워요. '철자가 틀리다', '철자를 맞게 쓰다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 철자 is how a word is spelled. Korean more often uses 맞춤법, which is the whole set of writing rules, while 철자 is closer to how one specific word is written. You say 철자가 틀리다 or 철자를 맞게 쓰다.
